## Before you start {.study}

- **What you need:** your three project files from lectures 28 and 29
  (`project.xlsx`, `report.docx`, `talk.pptx`), your feedback notes, Word,
  Excel and PowerPoint, and an AI tool your university allows.
- **Time:** about 60 minutes. Work alone, at your own speed.
- **How it works:** do Steps 1–3 on this page. Each step has a short text, a
  simulator and a self-check. Then do the **Tasks to submit**.
- **What you submit:** the final versions of the three files and an
  AI-use statement for the whole project.

![Three files and one statement.](images/final-checklist.png){width=100%}

## Key terms {.study}

{{< glossary course-project data-sheet final-version peer-feedback chart linked-object check-ai-output ai-use-statement >}}

## Step 1 · The final data sheet {.study}

- One clean **table**: one row per record, no empty rows, the same
  spelling in each column.
- A **formula** column (for example Total = Qty × Price) and a total row.
- A **summary** (a PivotTable or SUMIF) and **one chart** that answers
  your question, with a title and axis labels.

{{< sim file="../week-07/sims/chart-lab.html" poster="../week-07/sims/chart-lab.png" title="Chart Lab: the right chart for the question" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · The data sheet"}
Use Chart Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a pie with 20 slices|a table of text"}
compare the totals of five items
:   a column chart

the totals of four weeks in order
:   a line or column chart in week order

Total for 22 sandwiches at 1.5 JD
:   33 JD

an empty row in the middle
:   delete it
:::
:::

## Step 2 · The final report {.study}

- Keep the five **headings** (Heading 1): Introduction, The data, Results,
  What I learned, AI use.
- Update the **linked chart** (right-click › Update Link) and check every
  number in the text against Excel.
- Make **one change from the peer feedback** of lecture 29, and say which
  one under "What I learned".
- Check every AI sentence: is it true, shown by the data, and in your own
  words?

{{< sim file="../week-14/sims/link-lab.html" poster="../week-14/sims/link-lab.png" title="Link Lab: from Excel into Word" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The report"}
Use Link Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="type the numbers again|paste a screenshot"}
show the new Excel numbers in a linked chart
:   Update Link

a sentence with a number from AI
:   check it in Excel

the idea "Show the week totals too."
:   one change from the feedback

where you say which feedback you used
:   under "What I learned"
:::
:::

## Step 3 · The final slides and the AI-use statement {.study}

- Use the **four checks** on every slide: accuracy, claims, pictures,
  honesty (lecture 29).
- Keep **five slides** with speaker notes.
- Write one **AI-use statement** for the whole project: which AI tool, for
  what, and what you checked and changed. Put it at the end of the report
  and on slide 5.
- No personal data in any file or prompt.

{{< sim file="../week-12/sims/statement-builder.html" poster="../week-12/sims/statement-builder.png" title="Statement Builder: say how you used AI" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Slides and AI use"}
Use Statement Builder. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="nothing about AI|a password"}
451 JD on a slide, 415 JD in Excel
:   accuracy fails

"Everyone loves sandwiches."
:   claims fail

what an AI-use statement names
:   the tool, the use, the check

never in a file or a prompt
:   personal data
:::
:::

## Tasks to submit {.tasks}

Do the tasks alone. Your teacher marks them (10 marks). Use your own
project from lectures 28 and 29, and the file names below.

### Task 1 · The data sheet (3 marks)

Finish `project.xlsx`: one clean table with a formula column and a total
row, a summary (a PivotTable or SUMIF formulas), and one chart with a
title and axis labels that answers your question.

### Task 2 · The report (3 marks)

Finish `report.docx`: the five headings, the updated chart, two or three
checked insights with numbers, and one change from the peer feedback.

Which feedback did you use, and what did you change?

{{< answer-space lines=3 >}}

### Task 3 · The slides (2 marks)

Finish `talk.pptx`: five slides with speaker notes that pass the four
checks (accuracy, claims, pictures, honesty).

### Task 4 · AI use (2 marks)

Write your AI-use statement for the whole project (two or three
sentences), and put it at the end of the report and on slide 5. Then
answer: which AI output did you change or delete, and why?

{{< answer-space lines=4 >}}

## How to submit

Upload `project.xlsx`, `report.docx` and `talk.pptx` to the university
e-learning platform, by the date given there.
